mcqs.question: What is the OWASP Top 10 primarily built from?
options: A closed-door vote among OWASP's core maintainers
Contributed vulnerability-scan data from many organizations plus an industry practitioner survey
The CVE database filtered to the ten highest CVSS scores
Bug bounty payout totals across major platforms
mcqs.explanation: The list blends broad contributed scan/test data across hundreds of thousands of apps with a practitioner survey that surfaces categories the raw data under-represents, like Insecure Design. It isn't a closed vote, a CVSS filter, or a bounty-payout ranking.

mcqs.question: In the 2021 OWASP Top 10, which category ranks #1, displacing Injection?
options: Security Misconfiguration
Cryptographic Failures
Broken Access Control
Vulnerable & Outdated Components
mcqs.explanation: Broken Access Control took the top spot in 2021, both because such bugs are common and because tooling got better at detecting IDOR and missing-authorization patterns. Injection, which had topped every prior list, dropped to #3 as parameterized queries became the framework default.

mcqs.question: A team's scan comes back with zero OWASP Top 10 findings. What does that actually establish?
options: The application meets a minimum bar against ten known high-impact categories, not a complete security review
The application has no security vulnerabilities of any kind
The application's business logic has been fully threat-modeled
No further security testing is required before shipping
mcqs.explanation: The Top 10 is explicitly a floor: ten categories, not every CWE, and not business-logic abuse cases at all. A clean scan says those ten categories are covered — it says nothing about custom logic flaws or risks the list doesn't track.

mcqs.question: Why did Injection's rank fall between the 2017 and 2021 editions of the list?
options: SQL injection was declared out of scope for the 2021 edition
OWASP switched from data-driven ranking to a pure practitioner vote
Injection attacks stopped being exploitable in modern frameworks
The proportion of apps affected shrank as parameterized queries and ORMs became the default, even though injection bugs still occur
mcqs.explanation: The list tracks incidence data, and framework defaults shifted toward parameterized queries, lowering injection's relative share of findings. It wasn't removed from scope, OWASP didn't change its methodology to a pure vote, and injection is still very much exploitable where raw queries persist.

mcqs.question: A coupon-code endpoint lets a user apply the same discount code twice by replaying a request. Which OWASP Top 10 category does this fall under?
options: Security Misconfiguration, since the endpoint should have rate limiting
None of them — it's a business-logic flaw the category list doesn't name
Broken Access Control, since it involves an endpoint
Injection, since the coupon code is user-supplied input
mcqs.explanation: Replaying a coupon code isn't a weakness class the CWE-based Top 10 catalogs at all — it's an abuse of the application's own business rules, which is exactly the gap the list doesn't cover. It isn't a config, access-control, or injection bug even though it superficially touches an endpoint and user input.
